page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.xlarge is a general-purpose, burstable cloud instance based on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an x86_64 4th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz, it supplies 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory consists of 16.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, delivering 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides no bundled local instance storage and relies on network-attached storage, with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps and zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluation indicates solid performance in single-threaded tasks alongside burstable multi-core constraints. The instance achieves strong results in single-threaded gzip compression at 32.91 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 2498.0 points. Standard computing scores fall within median ranges, including a single-core Geekbench score of 1892.0, a multi-core score of 4435.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 7332.31. However, multi-threaded throughput under sustained load reflects typical burstable throttling, characterized by weak stress-ng multi-core performance (3944.96) and poor multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (12.0 GB/sec). Memory throughput and database operations also align with lower performance tiers, reaching 5.08 million operations per second on Redis SET operations.

The burstable CPU allocation provides cost efficiency for environments with fluctuating compute demand that do not continuously saturate CPU resources. Built-in support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets aids lightweight machine learning and vectorized tasks without the operational overhead of dedicated accelerators. Tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe storage, a 1 Gbps baseline network constraint, and lower sustained throughput during prolonged parallel computation. AWS m7i-flex.xlarge fits general web serving, application middleware, small-to-midsize databases, development environments, and batch processing tasks with variable utilization.

Its x86_64 architecture features 4 burstable vCPUs across 2 physical cores paired with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory. The instance includes no bundled local storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying on network-attached volumes alongside a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks show average single-core and general computational execution, highlighted by strong single-threaded gzip compression and text processing throughput. Multi-threaded processing and memory operations reveal performance degradation under sustained heavy utilization, corresponding to the burstable CPU allocation profile. Support for vector and matrix instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX enhances specific analytical operations. AWS m7i-flex.xlarge is designed for standard web serving, application staging, microservices, and variable-load batch operations.
